title: A Trilogy of Trilogies
text:
A Trilogy of Trilogies
Fliction comes in many lengths and forms, with numerous versions in between. The short story is out of vogue even though its exponents represent some of the best writers of the last century—O. Henry, Somerset Maugham, Scott Fitzgerald, Irwin Shaw, Ernest Hemingway and, I would submit, Jane Gardam, whose work is the main subject of this piece. These very good writers embraced the form, not exclusively, nor indeed with a view to writing a master work, but rather to get their hands quickly on much-needed money in a competitive world of letters.
The art of the short story has declined in tandem with the decline of the print medium in periodicals such as the Women’s Weekly and magazines that serialised the latest novels of well-known authors. Even Raymond Chandler or Dashiell Hammett would struggle to find a home for a short story in a magazine today—other than Quadrant.
